changelog:
Multi-view closes a cell whose decoder fails and says why, and the cells without sound let go of their streams while the app is in the background.

WHAT CHANGED

- Multi-view: when this device cannot start a decoder for a cell, runs out of decoders for it, or its decoders stop answering, the grid closes that cell and the note under the bar names the channel and says which of the three it was. The last cell in the grid is never closed this way: it keeps its message and its "Try again", as the player does.
- Multi-view: with the app in the background, the cells without sound stop and free their connections and decoders, and they start again at the live edge when you come back. The cell with the sound keeps playing, as the player does in the background. A cell that had given up stays as it was.
- After three reconnects within two minutes, the player turns on extra buffering for the rest of the session, from its next reconnect. It applies when the buffer setting is Low latency or Balanced; multi-view cells keep their own small buffer.
- A catalog refresh now reports the channels the app kept, not the ones the provider listed, and the source's summary says how many it skipped because the source already had them or listed them twice.
- The Continue Watching rail now shows when it arrives while you are at the top of the list. Before, it could be added just above the screen and never seen.
- Unpairing the television now keeps trying until the pairing service answers, including the next time the app starts. Before, it tried once.

WHAT STAYS THE SAME

- Everything from 0.5.13.1: a live channel whose provider closes the stream reconnecting by itself, multi-view's note about a provider's stream limit, a recording closing only the cells it needs, and the longer wait for a slow playlist.
